newsitem.title: USA: Au Bon Pain sees Q3 loss, $0.15-$0.20/shr.
newsitem.headline: Au Bon Pain sees Q3 loss, $0.15-$0.20/shr.

text.p: Au Bon Pain Co Inc said Thursday it expected a third quarter loss of between $0.15 and $0.20 a share.
The company attributed the loss to start-up costs of a new frozen dough production plant in MIssouri and federal tax law changes.
The company said it now expects to report a net loss for the 13 weeks ended October 5, 1996, of between $1.7 million and $2.4 million, or between $0.15 and $0.20 per share.

In addition, it announced it is evaluating whether to write down goodwill and certain other assets under FAS 121 during the quarter. Retail bakery cafe performance during the third quarter of 1996 is expected to be mixed, as comparable restaurant sales versus the third quarter of 1995 at the Au Bon Pain business unit have decreased about 3 percent, while at the Saint Louis Bread business unit the comparable restaurant sales have increased about 10 percent.

In the third quarter of 1996, the company began a transition to its new frozen dough plant in Mexico, Missouri. Significant problems encountered in the startup phase of the plant in establishing consistent production levels will result in significantly higher cost of food during the third quarter.

Food cost performance also continues to be hurt by continued high flour and even higher butter costs. In addition, operating results in the third quarter of 1996 are expected to include a 1996 year-to-date reduction of tax benefits recognized under the company's COLI program. This is the result of legislative changes in federal tax law adopted as part of the recently enacted Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act.

The company said in a statement that, "The combination of the costs of the startup of the manufacturing plant and the changes in tax legislation associated with the COLI program is extremely unfortunate. However, these costs do not effect the company's long-term economics."
